Add up only hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co, and leave out co2, oxygen and nitrogen. For each of the two samples, give me the timestamp, each gas value and the total. State which IEEE C57.104 condition level each total falls in, using these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630. Then give the change in TDCG in ppm/day between the two samples. If either sample is missing any of the six gases, don't use it. Move to the next earliest or next latest complete sample, and tell me which timestamps you ended up using.

Both endpoint samples contain all six gases; no replacements were needed. All values below are **ppm**.

| Gas / result | 2024-01-15T00:00:00.000000 | 2024-01-19T00:00:00.000000 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Hydrogen | 2,845 | 2,850 |
| Methane | 7,406 | 7,400 |
| Ethane | 5,467 | 5,470 |
| Ethylene | 16,684 | 16,650 |
| Acetylene | 7 | 7 |
| CO | 32 | 32 |
| **TDCG** | **32,441** | **32,409** |
| **IEEE C57.104 condition** | **4 (>4,630 ppm)** | **4 (>4,630 ppm)** |

CO₂, oxygen and nitrogen were excluded.

**TDCG change:** (32,409 − 32,441) ÷ 4 days = **−8 ppm/day** (a decrease).
